text: How does Levine's 'explanatory gap,' as he originally framed it, differ from Chalmers' hard problem?
choices: Levine's gap is an epistemological claim (we cannot explain why a neural state feels as it does) compatible with physicalism being true, whereas Chalmers draws the metaphysical conclusion that consciousness is non-physical
Levine argues consciousness is non-physical, while Chalmers holds it is physical
There is no difference; the two are exactly the same claim
Levine denies that qualia exist, whereas Chalmers affirms them
explanation: Levine (1983) claimed only that we cannot explain why a physical state has the qualitative character it does — an epistemic gap that could persist even if physicalism is true. Chalmers presses further to a metaphysical conclusion that phenomenal properties are not physical. Option 1 reverses their positions; option 2 ignores Levine's explicit caution; option 3 describes illusionism, not Levine.
